subject.title: BL-ecommerce-coupons-28: stripe bypass uses exact equality without rounding tolerance

question: Should ecommerce coupon checkout waive a residual payable amount up to 0.01 EUR and make that bypass decision authoritative through checkout?
rationale: The code fix is small, but the threshold changes payment behavior by writing off a residual amount and must be consistent between validation and the client checkout flow.

options.title: Waive up to one cent
options.body: Adopt the linked PR direction, ensure CheckoutContext consumes the same bypass rule, and document the coupon tolerance as business logic.

options.title: Keep exact payment accounting
options.body: Reject the tolerance and instead require Stripe/payment handling for any positive residual amount, even one cent.

options.title: Choose a different threshold
options.body: Ask for a revised PR with the exact finance-approved tolerance and tests for the chosen boundary.

recommendation.title: Waive up to one cent
recommendation.body: Adopt the linked PR direction, ensure CheckoutContext consumes the same bypass rule, and document the coupon tolerance as business logic.

likelyOwner.reason: MiguelHamelyn introduced the related coupon behavior and reported this BL divergence, so they are the best available business/code owner for the tolerance decision.
